userStories.title: Feature-scoped flow jobs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist feature identity on flow jobs and scope the engine's job reads without changing single-feature behavior.

**Motivation** — A flow created with two or more features is accepted, approved, and then never advanced: `listAdvanceable` filters on a feature count of 1 and `decideFlowStep` returns `skip` when `featureCount !== 1`.

**Approach** — Migration `20261203090000_fleet_flow_features`: `FleetJob.flowFeatureId String?` with `@@index([flowId, flowFeatureId, queuedAt])`, backfilled from the position-0 feature of each job's flow; `FleetFlowFeature.branch String?`; `FleetFlow.setSha String`, backfilled from `specSha`. `FleetJobsService.dispatch` writes `opts.flowFeatureId`; `adoptForFlow` takes the feature id (service, repository and `FleetJobRecord`/domain interface). The step repository's job reads take a `featureId` as their second argument and filter on `flowFeatureId`. The advance service passes `flow.features[0].id` everywhere (single-feature behaviour unchanged).

**Jobs are scoped to a feature by a new `FleetJob.flowFeatureId` column**, not by `FleetJob.feature`: a REVIEW job's `feature` is the canonical PR feature (`prNumberOfReviewFeature`), not the nax feature name. The migration backfills every existing flow job to its flow's position-0 feature, so single-feature flows read the same jobs.

Preserve the one-statement latest-job/own-lease ingest snapshot and queuedAt/id ordering. Write flowFeatureId at the dispatch insert only when flowId is supplied; adoption writes all three links in the same conditional update. Update all production callers and positional test doubles/assertions, including negative assertions, exact dispatch options and REVIEW adoption. Add setSha to direct Prisma fixtures as required by the schema; US-002 owns the repository's setSha update lifecycle. Exercise actual backfill with rows seeded before applying the migration using scratchSchemaBefore/applyMigration.

**Scope** — In: schema, SQL backfill/index, job domain/create data, dispatch/adoption, feature-scoped reads and single-feature engine wiring. Out: active feature selection (US-008), feature progression and sha-write semantics (US-002), later-feature start and merge polling (US-011/012).

**Interface** — `latestJobWithIngest(flowId, featureId)`, `latestJobForStep(flowId, featureId, step)`, `countJobsForStepSince(flowId, featureId, step, since)` filter on `FleetJob.flowFeatureId`; `adoptForFlow(jobId, flowId, flowFeatureId, step)`, writing `flowFeatureId` in the same conditional update. `FleetJobsService.dispatch(actorId, projectId, dto, opts)` also accepts `opts.flowFeatureId`, written with `flowId`.

userStories.title: Feature branch and state persistence
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist feature branches/states and separate the approved set sha from the first feature's changing spec sha.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, G6 and Steps 2.6) splits one brainstorm into several specs and carries them to ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — `FleetFlowFeatureRecord.branch`; step repository `setFeatureBranch`, `markFeatureState`, `setFlowState`; `complete` leaves `MERGED` features `MERGED`; `recordCalls` with a null sha leaves `flow.specSha`, and with `setSha: true` also moves `flow.setSha`; `PrismaFleetFlowRepository` writes `setSha` with `specSha` on create, re-ask and `updateSha`.

**A new `FleetFlow.setSha` holds the set's sha.** `flow.specSha` moves with the first feature's `PRD_REVIEW` calls (the re-PLAN preflight needs that), so after feature 1's PRD round it points at a commit that carries feature 1's `prd.json`. `setSha` is written wherever the flow repository writes `specSha` from outside the flow (create, re-ask, re-publish) and by `SPEC_REVIEW` calls, never by `PRD_REVIEW` calls. The `base: 'spec'` start and the spec blob check use `setSha`. `PRD_REVIEW` calls and PRD edits of a later feature are committed on that feature's branch and move neither sha.

**New feature states** `READY` (ready PR) and `MERGED`. A flow completes when no feature is `PENDING` and none is active; completion sets every non-`MERGED` feature to `COMPLETED` (a single-feature flow ends `COMPLETED`, as today).

Retain row-spreading mapping; add setSha to the flow domain record and optional nullable branch to the feature record. State writers mutate only the addressed row; activities/orchestration belong to later stories. Preserve complete's existing rejection when the flow is missing, before any feature completion writes. Null sha records the calls marker without either sha changing even if setSha promotion is requested. Verify persisted values through real repository reads.

**Scope** — In: domain mappings, feature/flow state and branch writers, completion persistence, calls sha promotion, create/reask/updateSha lifecycle. Out: schema migration (US-001), next-feature selection (US-004), orchestration/activity emission (US-008/009/010).

**Interface** — `recordCalls(flowId, featureId, jobId, specSha: string | null, options?: { setSha?: boolean })`: a non-null `specSha` moves `flow.specSha`, and with `setSha: true` also `flow.setSha`. New: `setFeatureBranch(featureId, branch)`, `markFeatureState(featureId, state)`, `setFlowState(flowId, state)`. `FleetFlowFeatureRecord` gains `branch?: string | null`.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] A flow read through IFleetFlowRepository.findById returns each feature's branch (null until set).
[integration] setFeatureBranch(featureId, 'feat/b') persists branch 'feat/b' on that feature only.
[integration] markFeatureState(featureId, 'READY') persists the feature's state 'READY' and leaves the other features and the flow state unchanged.
[integration] setFlowState(flowId, 'WAITING_MERGE') persists the flow state and leaves the features unchanged.
[integration] complete(flowId, now) on a flow with one MERGED and one READY feature sets the flow COMPLETED with endedAt now, leaves the MERGED feature MERGED and sets the READY feature COMPLETED.
[integration] recordCalls(flowId, featureId, jobId, null) sets the feature's callsJobId and leaves flow.specSha and flow.setSha unchanged.
[integration] recordCalls(flowId, featureId, jobId, 'sha2') sets the feature's callsJobId and flow.specSha 'sha2' and leaves flow.setSha unchanged.
[integration] recordCalls(flowId, featureId, jobId, 'sha3', { setSha: true }) sets both flow.specSha and flow.setSha to 'sha3'.
[integration] PrismaFleetFlowRepository.updateSha(id, 'sha4') and reask(id, { specSha: 'sha4', ... }) each set both specSha and setSha to 'sha4', and a created flow has setSha equal to its specSha.
[integration] complete('missing-flow', now) rejects and leaves unrelated flow and feature rows unchanged, preserving the existing missing-flow rejection before feature completion writes.

userStories.title: Flow branch rule for later features
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reject NAX flow inputs whose branch collides with a later feature's reserved feat branch.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, G6 and Steps 2.6) splits one brainstorm into several specs and carries them to ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — `parseFlowInput` (nax entry) rejects a later feature whose `feat/<feature>` equals the flow branch.

**`dependsOn` already names only earlier features**: `parseFlowInput` rejects a dependency it has not seen yet, so positions are the run order. New: for the nax entry, no feature after the first may have `feat/<feature>` equal to the flow branch (a create-time 400); the branch check runs where `branch` is validated, after the features.

One new validation failure is raised through its `fail(property)` helper (`ValidationAppException` with `reason` = the property path). A `dependsOn` naming the feature itself or a later feature is already rejected. Do not change THREAD normalization or existing validation/normalization order.

**Scope** — In: NAX create-input branch collision rule and existing parser tests. Out: dependency validation redesign (already implemented), GitHub branch creation/conflict resolution (US-005/011).

**Interface** — `parseFlowInput(body, entry)`; fail with `features.<position>.feature` for a later feature collision.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] parseFlowInput(body, 'NAX') with branch feat/b and features [a, b] throws ValidationAppException with reason features.1.feature.
[unit] parseFlowInput(body, 'NAX') with branch feat/a and features [a, b] accepts the input (the first feature may use its own feat/<feature> as the flow branch).

routing.reasoning: One additive parser check uses the existing validation helper and does not change authentication or authorization.

userStories.title: Forge branch creation and repo default branch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add idempotency-aware GitHub branch creation and expose the repository default branch to flow passes.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, G6 and Steps 2.6) splits one brainstorm into several specs and carries them to ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — `GitHubAppClient.createBranch(token, owner, name, branch, sha)` and `FleetReposService.findReviewRepo` returning `defaultBranch`.

**The API creates each later feature's branch** (`GitHubAppClient.createBranch`, `POST /git/refs`) before its `PLAN`, because a flow `PLAN` carries `expectBranch: job.ref` (`assign-payload.ts:67`) and the runner refuses a PRD whose `branchName` differs from the ref. No runner change.

POST `/repos/<owner>/<name>/git/refs` through the existing FleetHttpClient with `{ ref: 'refs/heads/<branch>', sha }`. A 201 returns created. On 422, probe getBranchHead and return exists with the observed sha; if that probe throws repo_not_found because the branch does not exist, return refused. Preserve other probe failures for classification by callers. Map HTTP 403/404/500 to app_permissions_insufficient/repo_not_found/provider_error. Do not log or persist the bearer token. The caller, not this client method, decides whether an existing branch's sha is acceptable.

`FleetReposService.findReviewRepo(id)` target: the pick also includes `defaultBranch`. Keep the narrow projection, and update its equality test and the typed reviewRepo fixture in fleet-flow-calls.service.spec.ts with defaultBranch: 'main'.

**Scope** — In: GitHub client operation, response/error mapping, repo projection and affected fixtures. Out: branch base selection/spec verification/creator checks (US-011), merge watch (US-012), runner changes.

**Interface** — `GitHubAppClient.createBranch(token, owner, name, branch, sha)` returns `{ kind: 'created' }`, `{ kind: 'exists', sha: <head> }`, or `{ kind: 'refused' }`; `findReviewRepo(id)` returns `Pick<FleetRepoRecord, 'id' | 'projectId' | 'owner' | 'name' | 'githubInstallationId' | 'defaultBranch'> | null` asynchronously.

[unit] On HTTP 422, createBranch reads getBranchHead for feat/b and returns { kind: 'exists', sha: <head> }.
[unit] On HTTP 403, createBranch throws RepoCheckException with app_permissions_insufficient.
[unit] On HTTP 404, createBranch throws RepoCheckException with repo_not_found.
[unit] On HTTP 500, createBranch throws RepoCheckException with provider_error.
[unit] FleetReposService.findReviewRepo(id) returns the repo's defaultBranch with the existing id, projectId, owner, name and githubInstallationId review projection fields.
[unit] On HTTP 422 when getBranchHead for feat/b throws RepoCheckException with repo_not_found (the branch does not exist), createBranch returns { kind: 'refused' }.

routing.reasoning: Existing HTTP integration patterns are straightforward, but bearer-token handling and forge permission classification require the security override.

userStories.title: Step decision for later features
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make first-feature review entry distinct from later-feature PLAN entry in the pure step decision.

**Motivation** — A flow created with two or more features is accepted, approved, and then never advanced: `listAdvanceable` filters on a feature count of 1 and `decideFlowStep` returns `skip` when `featureCount !== 1`.

**Approach** — `decideFlowStep` takes `firstFeature` instead of `featureCount`; the advance service's `decisionInput` passes `firstFeature: true` (it still reads `flow.features[0]` until US-008). The new stop reasons `pr_closed` and `spec_changed` join `FlowStopReason`.

`featureCount` replaced by `firstFeature: boolean`; no skip; with a null latest job, the first feature dispatches `SPEC_REVIEW` and a later feature dispatches `PLAN`; `state === 'APPROVED'` handling applies to the first feature only.

**The set's `SPEC_REVIEW` belongs to the first feature** (`flowFeatureId` = position 0). Later features start at `PLAN`.

Retain all other completed PLAN, PRD_REVIEW, RUN ingest, REVIEW/RULE, answer, failure and FIX readiness behavior, including already-ready FIX results. Replace the old multi-feature skip test with later-feature PLAN entry, and update both advance decision-input assertions from featureCount: 1 to firstFeature: true.

**Scope** — In: decision input/branch rules, stop reason union and interim first-feature service adapter. Out: selecting the active feature (US-008), READY/merge transitions (US-009/012).

**Interface** — `decideFlowStep(input: FlowStepInput)` with `firstFeature: boolean` instead of `featureCount`; `FlowStopReason` adds `'pr_closed' | 'spec_changed'`.

[unit] decideFlowStep with firstFeature: true, state RUNNING and no latest job returns { kind: 'dispatch', step: 'SPEC_REVIEW' }.
[unit] decideFlowStep with firstFeature: true, state APPROVED and no latest job returns { kind: 'dispatch', step: 'SPEC_REVIEW' }.
[unit] decideFlowStep with firstFeature: false, state RUNNING and a completed PLAN job with a result branch and sha returns { kind: 'dispatch', step: 'PRD_REVIEW' }.
[unit] decideFlowStep with firstFeature: false, state RUNNING and a completed FIX job whose fixReady.markedReady is true returns { kind: 'complete' }.
[unit] For a single-feature flow, FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance passes a decision input with firstFeature true and no featureCount field.

[unit] decideFlowStep with state RUNNING and a completed PLAN job missing resultBranch or resultSha returns { kind: 'stop', reason: 'plan_no_result', detail: 'PLAN job has no result branch or sha' } for either firstFeature value, preserving the existing incomplete-PLAN guard.

routing.reasoning: Localized pure decision and input-adapter changes retain the existing step state machine.

userStories.title: Set review task, per-feature findings, dispatch input and calls target
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make set-wide review tasks and explicit per-feature dispatch/commit targets available to the advance engine.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, G6 and Steps 2.6) splits one brainstorm into several specs and carries them to ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — `parseFlowVerdict` keeps a finding's `feature`; `buildReviewTask` builds the set task from `setSpecPaths`; `buildStepDispatch` forwards `setSpecPaths` and plans from `feature.branch`; `FleetFlowCallsService.apply` and `applyPrdEdits` take a `target`. The advance service passes `{ feature, specPath, branch: flow.branch }` of `flow.features[0]` as the target until US-008.

Each `SPEC_REVIEW` round is one AGENT job over the whole set: it names every spec path and asks for cross-spec consistency. Its calls and questions may target any feature's spec.

`FlowFinding` / `parseFlowVerdict`: an optional string `feature` field is kept on each finding when present. `buildReviewTask(step, specPath, feature, options)` where `options.setSpecPaths?: string[]` (two or more paths) makes the `SPEC_REVIEW` task name every spec path, ask for cross-spec consistency, and ask each finding to carry `"feature":"<feature>"`. Preserve exact prior task output without set paths and keep the verdict suffix whole under AGENT_TASK_MAX_LENGTH. A non-string finding.feature is omitted without dropping its finding.

`PLAN` uses `input.feature.branch ?? flow.branch` as its ref; `SPEC_REVIEW` forwards `input.setSpecPaths` to `buildReviewTask`; the advance service sets `setSpecPaths` to every feature's spec path in position order when the flow has two or more features (that population belongs to US-008). Explicit calls targets replace hardcoded flow.features[0] and flow.branch for reads, writes, PRD path and commit messages, preserving pinned-head, conflict/retry and already-applied behavior. Use the target.feature for `.nax/features/<feature>/prd.json`. All existing three-argument apply/applyPrdEdits callers and assertions gain the fourth argument now.

**Scope** — In: verdict/parser, set prompt, dispatch builder inputs/ref and explicit calls-service target with interim first-feature caller wiring. Out: selecting active features (US-008), grouping/multiple commits (US-010), branch creation (US-011). Runner changes remain excluded.

**Interface** — `buildReviewTask(step, specPath, feature, options)` adds `options.setSpecPaths?: string[]`; `BuildStepDispatchInput.feature: { feature: string; specPath: string; branch?: string | null }` and a top-level `setSpecPaths?: string[]`. Both `FleetFlowCallsService.apply(flow, action, expectedHead)` and `applyPrdEdits(flow, action, expectedHead)` take a fourth argument `target: { feature: string; specPath: string; branch: string }`.

[unit] buildStepDispatch for SPEC_REVIEW with input setSpecPaths: ['.nax/features/a/spec.md', '.nax/features/b/spec.md'] returns an agent.task naming both paths.
[unit] buildStepDispatch for PLAN with feature.branch 'feat/b' returns ref 'feat/b'.
[unit] buildStepDispatch for PLAN with feature.branch null or absent returns ref flow.branch.
[unit] FleetFlowCallsService.apply(flow, action, head, { feature: 'b', specPath: '.nax/features/b/spec.md', branch: 'feat/b' }) reads getBranchHead of feat/b and getFile of .nax/features/b/spec.md.

userStories.title: Advance runs the active feature
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Drive the existing step chain using the selected feature's identity, jobs, markers, branch and payloads.

**Motivation** — A flow created with two or more features is accepted, approved, and then never advanced: `listAdvanceable` filters on a feature count of 1 and `decideFlowStep` returns `skip` when `featureCount !== 1`.

**Approach** — `decide`'s single-feature early return is removed and `listAdvanceable` lists flows of any feature count. `FleetFlowAdvanceService` selects the active feature with `nextFlowFeature` and carries it as `DispatchPass.feature` to the decision, `dispatchStep`, the calls, rulings and PRD-edit passes, the stop payload and the waiting payload; the spec preflight runs only for the first feature; a later feature's `PRD_REVIEW` calls and PRD edits target its own branch and move no sha; a later feature's `stale` calls or PRD-edits outcome stops `spec_changed`.

**The spec preflight belongs to the first feature.** `readSpecHead` and the `SPEC_REVIEW`/`PLAN` spec-sha check in `decide` compare the flow branch head with `flow.specSha`; once feature 1 has run, that branch carries its PLAN, RUN and FIX commits. Both run only while the active feature is the first; a later feature's spec was checked by its start pass.

The active feature reaches `dispatchStep` and the calls, rulings and PRD-edit passes as a new `feature` field on `DispatchPass` (a `FleetFlowFeatureRecord`); `dispatchStep` builds the body from `pass.feature`, not `flow.features[0]`.

userStories.title: Feature completion and the next-feature transitions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Turn a ready step outcome into feature readiness and the next ordered flow transition atomically.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, G6 and Steps 2.6) splits one brainstorm into several specs and carries them to ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — The step decision's `complete` marks the active feature `READY` and applies `nextFlowFeature` in the same transaction (flow `COMPLETED`, `WAITING_MERGE`, or left `RUNNING`); a live flow with no active and no pending feature completes.

The step decision's `complete` for the active feature marks it `READY` (activity `flow.feature_ready`) and then applies `nextFlowFeature` in the same transaction: `complete` completes the flow, `wait_merge` moves it to `WAITING_MERGE`, `start` leaves it `RUNNING` for the next pass.

An `APPROVED`/`RUNNING` flow decides with `nextFlowFeature`. `active`: the existing step decision, fed with the active feature's own jobs, ids and branch. `start`: the **start pass**. `complete`: complete the flow. `wait_merge`: move the flow to `WAITING_MERGE` (activity `flow.waiting_merge`). This story records the transitions and leaves start execution to US-011.

**New feature states** `READY` (ready PR) and `MERGED`. A flow completes when no feature is `PENDING` and none is active; completion sets every non-`MERGED` feature to `COMPLETED` (a single-feature flow ends `COMPLETED`, as today).

Evaluate the next action from an updated in-memory feature view or locked re-read after marking READY; a stale snapshot must not select the just-finished feature again. Record flow.waiting_merge with awaited feature ids and flow.completed with the existing audit/activity pattern under the same parent/flow locks. A ready PR is sufficient for an independent successor; do not wait for unrelated PR merges or dispatch the next PLAN in the completion transaction. Preserve the existing pr_not_ready stop for a completed FIX carrying a CI readyHeld reason; that negative path must not enter the READY/completion branch.

**Scope** — In: per-feature READY, post-ready state decision, no-active/no-pending completion, activities and the existing CI-held FIX stop regression. Out: branch creation (US-011), polling/marking MERGED/resuming (US-012), parallel feature execution.

**Interface** — Consume `nextFlowFeature(features: readonly FlowFeatureView[]): FlowFeatureAction`; persist through `markFeatureState(featureId, state)`, `setFlowState(flowId, state)`, and `complete(flowId, now)`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When the active position-1 feature's latest completed FIX job has fixReady.markedReady true and its step is already recorded, advance calls markFeatureState(<position 1 id>, 'READY') and records activity flow.feature_ready.
[unit] When the step decision completes the position-0 feature and position 1 is independent, the flow stays RUNNING and steps.complete is not called.

[unit] When the step decision completes the position-0 feature and position 1 depends on it, setFlowState(flowId, 'WAITING_MERGE') is called and activity flow.waiting_merge is recorded with the awaited feature ids.
[unit] When the step decision completes the last feature, steps.complete is called and activity flow.completed is recorded.

userStories.title: Set SPEC_REVIEW calls pass
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Commit each set-wide SPEC_REVIEW finding into its target spec and record the set review atomically after all commits.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, G6 and Steps 2.6) splits one brainstorm into several specs and carries them to ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — The `apply_calls` pass for a multi-feature `SPEC_REVIEW` commits the findings spec by spec and records them.

`SPEC_REVIEW` calls for a set: the `apply_calls` pass groups the findings by `feature` (a missing or unknown name goes to the first feature), and commits one spec at a time in position order, each with `expectedHead` = the previous commit sha (the first: `flow.specSha`), on the flow branch. After the last commit, under the locks, `recordCalls` for every target feature, the last one moving `flow.specSha` and `flow.setSha` (`setSha: true`) to the last commit, and the first feature's `callsJobId` is set to the job id (the set marker the decision reads). The grouping is a pure function `groupFindingsByFeature(findings, features)` in `flow-features.ts`.

Keep all forge calls outside transactions; only after every targeted spec commits may the locked record phase write markers/shas/activity. Use null sha for non-final marker writes; the final target promotes both shas. Record the position-0 marker even when it has no findings, without committing an empty spec group. A failed call stops calls_failed and short-circuits later groups; retry writes no progress, so the next pass begins at the first group. A stale outcome while the first feature owns SPEC_REVIEW retains existing re-ask behavior. Keep existing single-file already-applied recovery; do not invent multi-commit crash recovery. Unknown feature names silently fall back to the first feature's spec. Preserve the existing single-feature calls target and one-call execution; every SPEC_REVIEW calls commit, including a single-feature pass, promotes setSha together with specSha. Setting the first feature's callsJobId moves past the applied job, not necessarily past the SPEC_REVIEW step: the existing round-count rule may request another set review before PLAN.

**Scope** — In: multi-feature SPEC_REVIEW grouping/commit chain, locked set markers and sha promotion, retry/failed behavior and single-feature calls regression. Out: later PRD_REVIEW behavior (US-008) and feature start/merge watch (US-011/012). Recovering a set `SPEC_REVIEW` calls pass in which two or more spec commits landed and nothing was recorded; the
  next pass sees a stale head and re-asks the flow (no feature is `READY` yet). A pass where only the first commit
  landed recovers through the existing already-applied check. US-010 only: a `SPEC_REVIEW` finding whose `feature` names no flow feature is not reported; it goes to the first
  feature's spec.

**Interface** — Consume `groupFindingsByFeature(findings, features)`, `calls.apply(flow, action, expectedHead, target)` with `target: { feature: string; specPath: string; branch: string }`, and `recordCalls(flowId, featureId, jobId, specSha: string | null, options?: { setSha?: boolean })`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] For a two-feature flow whose SPEC_REVIEW verdict has findings with feature a and b, the apply_calls pass calls calls.apply twice, first for a with expectedHead flow.specSha, then for b with expectedHead the commit sha of the first call.
[unit] Both calls in that pass target the flow branch, and each receives only the findings of its own feature.
[unit] A SPEC_REVIEW finding with no feature, or with a name no flow feature has, is committed into the first feature's spec.
[unit] After that pass, recordCalls is called for a and for b, the last call with the second commit's sha and { setSha: true }, and the first feature's callsJobId is the SPEC_REVIEW job id.
[unit] When the first apply of a set pass returns failed, the flow stops calls_failed and the second feature's apply is not called.
[unit] When the second apply returns retry, nothing is recorded and the next pass starts again from the first feature.

[unit] A set pass whose findings all target feature b commits only b's spec and still sets the first feature's callsJobId to the job id, so the next decision moves past this review without reapplying its calls (another SPEC_REVIEW round when specReviewCount < 2, otherwise PLAN).

userStories.title: Start pass for a later feature
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Safely create and record each later feature's branch from the approved set or merged default-branch head before PLAN.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, G6 and Steps 2.6) splits one brainstorm into several specs and carries them to ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — **Start pass** (`runFeatureStart` in `fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts`), outside any transaction, with one `mintInstallationToken` token: refuse a thread-entry flow (`dispatch_refused`, `thread entry runs one feature`); resolve the base sha (`spec`: `flow.setSha`; `default`: `getBranchHead` of the repo's `defaultBranch`); read the feature's spec file at the base and at `flow.setSha` and compare their blob shas (different or missing: stop `spec_changed`, detail `<specPath> differs from the approved spec`); create `feat/<feature>` at the base sha. Then under the locks, only if the feature is still `PENDING` at the locked re-read: `setFeatureBranch`, `markFeatureState(RUNNING)`, activity `flow.feature_started` with `{ feature, base, sha, branch }`. The next pass dispatches its `PLAN`.

The two new passes live in a new file `fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts` as functions that take the advance service's collaborators as arguments, so the service stays under 800 lines and its constructor does not change. This story owns the new module and start export; US-012 adds merge watch in the same module on the binding sibling dependency graph. Preserve sibling edits rather than overwriting the module.

**Tokens (my call).** Merge watch reads PRs with `mintThreadReadToken` (contents, pull_requests and metadata read): `mintReadOnlyToken` has no `pull_requests` grant and gets a 403 on a private repo (`fleet-pr-rulings.service.ts:42`). The start pass uses `mintInstallationToken` (contents write) for every call, because `POST /git/refs` needs `contents: write`.

**Forge errors are classified as the calls already are** (`callsOutcomeForForgeError`): a `RepoCheckException` with reason `app_not_installed`, `app_permissions_insufficient` or `repo_not_found` stops the flow `dispatch_refused` with the reason as detail; any other reason ends the pass and the next tick retries.

Creator lost dispatch access at the start pass: stop `creator_lost_access` before any forge call. Repo has no GitHub installation (not connected): stop `dispatch_refused`, detail `repo not connected`. Same-base existing branch is treated as created. Existing branch at another sha: stop `dispatch_refused`, detail `branch feat/<feature> already exists`. Refused creation (422 with no branch, invalid base): stop `dispatch_refused`, detail `branch feat/<feature> not created`. Spec comparisons use blob shas, not commit shas, and use setSha, not specSha. Mint one token for all forge operations in the pass; never persist/log it. On transient failure, write nothing. Record under parent then flow locks only for the same approval generation and still-live/PENDING selected feature; a stopped flow, changed approvedAt or already-started feature drops external progress. Every unit acceptance criterion drives FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance, not the helper directly.

**Scope** — In: runFeatureStart wiring, permission guard, repo/base/spec checks, forge branch operation consumption, locked record/activity and preservation of the first feature's existing SPEC_REVIEW entry without branch creation. Out: merge watch (US-012) and job dispatch (next pass via US-008). Stacked PRs: building a feature on another feature's unmerged branch. Multi-feature thread-entry flows: they stop at the second feature's start. Rebasing, merging or updating a feature branch when the default branch moves; a conflict fails a job and stops
  the flow like any failure. A crash between `createBranch` and its record on a `base: 'default'` start, after which the default branch moves:
  the repeat finds the branch at the old sha and stops `dispatch_refused`; the flow is cloned.

**Interface** — `runFeatureStart` is a collaborator-taking function in `fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts`, consumed by `FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance`; `GitHubAppClient.createBranch(token, owner, name, branch, sha)` and `FleetReposService.findReviewRepo(id)` with `defaultBranch` supply the forge seam.

userStories.title: Merge watch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Poll awaited PRs for WAITING_MERGE flows, persist merges and resume or stop without dispatching jobs.

**Motivation** — The fleet flow design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, G6 and Steps 2.6) splits one brainstorm into several specs and carries them to ready PRs with one approval.

**Approach** — A `WAITING_MERGE` flow runs **merge watch** (`runMergeWatch` in `fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts`): outside any transaction, mint a token with `mintThreadReadToken` and call `getPullRequest` for each awaited feature's `prNumber`. `merged: true` marks the feature `MERGED`; `state: 'closed'` with `merged: false`, or a null result, stops the flow `pr_closed` with detail `PR #<n> closed without merge` or `PR #<n> not found`; an open PR changes nothing. Then, under the locks, write the merges and, when `nextFlowFeature` now returns `start`, move the flow to `RUNNING` (activity `flow.resumed`).

The record transaction re-reads the flow under the parent and flow locks and writes only while it is still `WAITING_MERGE` with the same `approvedAt`. The two new passes live in a new file `fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts` as functions that take the advance service's collaborators as arguments, so the service stays under 800 lines and its constructor does not change. US-011 owns creation of the shared file, but is a sibling, not a binding dependency: coordinate adding runMergeWatch without overwriting runFeatureStart; do not alter the required story dependency list.

**Tokens (my call).** Merge watch reads PRs with `mintThreadReadToken` (contents, pull_requests and metadata read): `mintReadOnlyToken` has no `pull_requests` grant and gets a 403 on a private repo (`fleet-pr-rulings.service.ts:42`). The start pass uses `mintInstallationToken` (contents write) for every call, because `POST /git/refs` needs `contents: write`.

**Forge errors are classified as the calls already are** (`callsOutcomeForForgeError`): a `RepoCheckException` with reason `app_not_installed`, `app_permissions_insufficient` or `repo_not_found` stops the flow `dispatch_refused` with the reason as detail; any other reason ends the pass and the next tick retries.

`listAdvanceable` also lists `WAITING_MERGE` flows; retain APPROVED/RUNNING flows of any feature count, id paging and exclusions for PENDING/WAITING_ANSWER/terminal flows. Select awaited ids with nextFlowFeature; poll only named dependencies still unmerged. Missing installation stops dispatch_refused (`repo not connected`); awaited READY without prNumber stops dispatch_refused (`feature <feature> has no PR`). Collect forge results outside any transaction, including token minting; a transient failure writes nothing. Under the locked, same-generation WAITING_MERGE re-read, persist partial merges even when another dependency is open, and use flows.stop for pr_closed with normal activity/audit/outbox. Never dispatch in merge watch even if every dependency merges; resume first, start on the next pass. Every unit acceptance criterion drives FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance.

**Scope** — In: WAITING_MERGE eligibility, runMergeWatch, read-token polling, partial merge persistence, fenced resume/stop, failure classification. Out: branch creation (US-011), webhook-driven merge detection, merging/rebasing PRs, web/CLI displays.

userStories.title: Two-feature flows against the database
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Demonstrate the complete ordered independent and dependent feature lifecycles through the real ticker and database with a stubbed forge.

**Motivation** — A flow created with two or more features is accepted, approved, and then never advanced: `listAdvanceable` filters on a feature count of 1 and `decideFlowStep` returns `skip` when `featureCount !== 1`.

**Approach** — An integration spec driving `FleetFlowTicker.tick` for two nax-entry flows with the forge stubbed: an independent second feature that starts at the first's ready PR, and a dependent second feature that waits for the first's merge.

One feature is active at a time. An independent feature (no `dependsOn`) starts as soon as the previous feature reaches a ready PR; it does not wait for a merge. A dependent feature waits (`WAITING_MERGE`) until every feature it names is merged.

Feature 1 keeps the flow branch. A dependent feature plans from the default branch after its dependencies are merged; an independent feature plans from the flow's spec sha. Each later feature gets its own `feat/<feature>` branch and PR. For the independent base, use the stable `flow.setSha` defined by the set-sha ruling, not the first feature's later PRD-bearing specSha.

Use the real flow repository, dispatch path, permissions and FleetFlowTicker; manually settle each dispatched job and required ingest/PR fields in the test to progress the chain. Stub forge calls, not nextFlowFeature or the step decision. Mirror fleet-flow-verdicts.integration.spec.ts and fleet-fixtures.ts: disable background sweep/outbox relay, create isolated repo/creator/runner fixtures, make explicit ticks, and record the transaction probe for every token/forge stub. Use the transaction manager's existing isInTransaction() behind the test's inTransaction probe. Assert independent b starts despite a moved flow-branch head; use distinct setSha/specSha/default-head values so the correct base is observable. Verify the closed-unmerged dependent case with an isolated instance or fixture reset rather than trying to restart a stopped flow. Gate real PostgreSQL using canRunDbTests, require KODA_DB_TESTS=1 outside the sandbox, and run the scoped integration suite on a private test database; a skip is not verification. This test-only story is explicitly binding and remains separate from implementation stories.
